newsitem.title: UK: Wolseley hits 7-month low on sterling woes.
newsitem.headline: Wolseley hits 7-month low on sterling woes.

text.p: Shares in Wolseley Plc touched a seven-month low on Wednesday as the international building supplies distributor became another victim of sterling's strength, dealers said.
Expectations for a hike in UK interest rates on Thursday also undercut the shares, they said.
At 1420 GMT Wolseley traded 17p lower at 428-1/2p, making it the second largest percentage loser in a generally stronger FTSE 100 market.
Shares in other building materials companies were mostly lower.
RMC Group Plc lost 4-1/2p to 889p, BPB Plc fell 3-1/2p to 297-1/2p and Hepworth Plc traded down 7p at 218-1/2p.
"I think if you point the finger at currency you won't go wrong and there is the potential base rate increase tomorrow," one market maker said. "But I think it's overdone right now."
The stock has dropped 16 percent from a high of 510p on June 13.
The rise in sterling, which touched a six-year peak against the German mark on Wednesday, has underscored fears over competitiveness and currency translation by companies operating overseas.
